lead: Ziegler-Natta polymerization builds linear, stereoregular polymers from alkenes by inserting one monomer at a time into a metal-carbon bond. A transition metal compound such as TiCl4 is activated by an alkyl aluminium such as Al(C2H5)3, reduced to solid TiCl3, and left with a vacant site. Propene gives largely isotactic polypropene; ethene gives linear high-density polyethylene. Industry uses it for bottles, pipes, films and automotive parts. Only a few universities teach this mechanism in detail.
prereq: You need: 5.2 for tacticity and 5.3 for chain growth.

blocks.text: TiCl4 is a transition metal compound. Al(C2H5)3, triethyl aluminium or AlEt3, is the alkyl aluminium co-catalyst. The aluminium compound is the activator: it alkylates titanium and reduces Ti(IV) to Ti(III). A simplified overall reaction is:

blocks.where: TiCl4 is titanium tetrachloride; Al(C2H5)3 is triethyl aluminium; TiCl3(s) is solid titanium trichloride; C2H4 is ethene and C2H6 is ethane, formed as by-products.

blocks.text: The solid TiCl3 has a surface. Each surface titanium ion has one vacant coordination position. This vacant site is the active centre. An alkene donates its pi electrons into it. The growing chain stays attached by a Ti-C bond.

items: Mix TiCl4 with Al(C2H5)3; solid TiCl3 particles form.
An ethyl group attaches to surface Ti, leaving one vacant position.
An alkene molecule coordinates at the vacant position.
The growing alkyl chain migrates to the bound alkene, making a new Ti-C bond and freeing the site.
The cycle repeats; each pass adds one monomer unit.

blocks.text: In insertion, the Ti-C bond breaks and a new Ti-C bond forms at the other end of the alkene. The chain shifts by one monomer unit. The vacant site returns, so the next alkene binds in the same way. This is coordination-insertion polymerization, a chain-growth method.

The solid surface is rigid. It allows the alkene to approach in only one orientation. For propene, the methyl group is forced to one side. Most repeat units therefore have the same tacticity: the polymer is largely isotactic. A small atactic fraction usually forms too and is removed in the plant. The same control gives linear high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Linear chains pack well, so HDPE is stiff and dense.

items: Metallocene catalysts are soluble single-site catalysts that follow the same coordination-insertion mechanism but are not Ziegler-Natta catalysts; they give very uniform polymers.
The Phillips process uses chromium oxide on silica to make HDPE.
Ziegler-Natta polypropene is used in car parts and woven sacks.

figure.caption: The catalyst is activated to a solid TiCl3 site; an alkene coordinates, the chain migrates, and the vacant site returns.

spec.aria: A top-to-bottom cycle from catalyst preparation to surface site, alkene binding, chain migration and isotactic polymer.

examples.question: Catalyst is prepared from TiCl4 (189.7 g/mol) and Al(C2H5)3 (114.2 g/mol) in 1:1 mole ratio. For a batch using 0.050 mol TiCl4, find the mass of each reagent, and the polymer mass if 1.0 kg propene is fed at 85% conversion.
steps: Moles of Al(C2H5)3 = moles of TiCl4 = 0.050 mol because the ratio is 1:1.
Mass of TiCl4 = 0.050 mol × 189.7 g/mol = 9.485 g ≈ 9.49 g.
examples.answer: TiCl4 = 9.49 g, Al(C2H5)3 = 5.71 g, and polymer = 850 g.
examples.check:
ti = 0.050
M_TiCl4 = 189.7
M_AlEt3 = 114.2
propene_feed_kg = 1.0
conversion = 0.85
print(round(ti * M_TiCl4, 2))
print(round(ti * M_AlEt3, 2))
print(round(conversion * propene_feed_kg * 1000, 1))

traps: The alkyl aluminium is the activator, not the polymerising centre; the transition metal site does the inserting.
Ziegler-Natta gives stereoregular polypropene, largely isotactic, not atactic polymer.
TiCl4 alone is not the active propene catalyst; it needs the alkyl aluminium and the solid TiCl3 surface.
Do not confuse this with free-radical addition; no radical initiator is used here.
85% conversion of 1.0 kg gives 850 g, not 0.85 g; keep the kilogram to gram change.

quiz.q: Name the two components of a Ziegler-Natta catalyst.
quiz.a: A transition metal compound such as TiCl4 and an alkyl aluminium such as Al(C2H5)3.

quiz.q: Why does solid TiCl3 give largely isotactic polypropene?
quiz.a: The rigid surface allows propene to bind in one orientation, so each insertion places the methyl group on the same side.

quiz.q: Using 0.020 mol TiCl4, find the mass of TiCl4 and Al(C2H5)3 needed. Molar masses: TiCl4 = 189.7 g/mol, Al(C2H5)3 = 114.2 g/mol.
A polypropene sample is fully atactic. Can it have come from this solid Ziegler-Natta catalyst? Explain.
quiz.a: No. The solid site controls orientation and gives mostly isotactic chains; atactic polymer points to a non-stereospecific route.

quiz.q: What is the role of the vacant coordination position on Ti?
quiz.a: It accepts the alkene pi electrons and starts the insertion cycle.

quiz.q: Why is Ziegler-Natta HDPE linear and stiff?
quiz.a: The catalyst gives little branching, so chains pack closely; strong packing makes the polymer stiff and dense.

beyond: Not for the exam. Metallocene catalysts are single-site versions that give narrow molar-mass distributions and fine stereocontrol. The Phillips chromium oxide process is a separate industrial route to HDPE. Reactor design and particle growth decide plant output. Search next for metallocene polyolefins and Phillips catalyst.
